cohort: Hospitalized patients at Universiti Kebangsaan Medical Centre (UKMMC) diagnosed with ST-elevated myocardial infarction (STEMI), elective lower segment caesarean section (LSCS), or elective total knee replacement (TKR) between June 2008 and December 2010.
finding: The implementation of clinical pathways was associated with a significantly lower mean length of stay for LSCS and STEMI patients without a significant increase in complication or readmission rates.
mod_finding: For elective lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) patients, the clinical pathway group had a lower mean length of stay (4.04 days) compared to the control group (4.99 days).
cross-section timing: Data was obtained for patients admitted from June 2008 to December 2010, comparing those managed before (June 2008-January 2009) and after (February 2009-December 2010) the implementation of clinical pathways.
